content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Repo indkhan/Moneo. GitHub issue #227 (read `gh issue view 227` with comments, and AGENTS.md), part 4 of 4: live words for the local ("On this computer") speech-to-text engine in the chat mic. Parts 1–3 are merged on main: the engine contract and fallback (PR #273/#279 area), the local transformers.js/onnxruntime-node engine in a server worker (PR #282), and OpenRouter (PR #291). Read `lib/ai/speech/` (engine.ts, registry.ts, the local engine and worker), the chat-mic client code in `components/chat-composer*` / voice hooks, and how the OpenAI engine shows live words today.

Goal: when the owner dictates with the local engine, words appear while they speak, like the OpenAI live engine, instead of only after they stop. Owner's decisions: chat mic only (never voice calls); local-first; must feel native. Suggested approach (simplify if something easier works): the client streams audio chunks to the server; the worker re-transcribes the growing buffer (or a sliding window) every ~1 s while recording and streams interim text back (e.g. SSE or a streamed response); the final transcript on stop is authoritative and replaces the interim text. Bound the work so a slow machine never queues up re-transcriptions (skip a tick while one is in flight). Vocabulary hints still apply. If the engine is missing or fails, the existing OpenAI fallback and note still work. OpenRouter stays batch-only.

Hit every surface: Settings (no new setting unless needed), desktop app (native module in the packaged app, `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/` for runtime paths, `desktop:build`), source install. Tests: the throttling/no-overlap logic and the interim→final replacement in `lib/` with fake timers; mock the model (no real model download in tests). Verify in the QA app (`npm run qa:server`, port 3100) if you can download a small model into a scratch `MONEO_DATA_DIR`; attach a short recording or screenshots via the verify-ui skill if feasible, else say so.

Create branch `t3/issue-227-live-words` from origin/main. Commit in steps with plain messages ending with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` yourself and quote their last lines. Run `npm run feature-map` if you add routes. Never touch the owner's backend (.env, Docker project `moneo`, port 3000) or their desktop app/user-data folder; never run `qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`; revert any migration you apply to moneo-qa. Real AI calls cost money: mock them. Never kill a process you didn't start (verify by PID). Don't end your turn while a command is still running. No comments in code. Open the PR (body ends with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)"), never merge it. Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>.

Speech to text on this computer (part 2 of #227)
Part 2 of #227 (does not close it).

## What changed

The chat mic can now turn speech into text **on this computer**. Voice calls and GPT-Live are untouched.

- **Runtime** (`lib/ai/speech/`): transformers.js (`@huggingface/transformers` 4.3) with onnxruntime-node, in a worker thread (`local-worker.mjs`, started with `new Worker(new URL(...))`). The model loads on first use and the worker ends after 5 idle minutes. A crashed worker fails the waiting recordings, and the next recording starts a fresh one.
  - Whisper gets the workspace vocabulary (`voice-vocabulary.ts`, shared through `promptWithNames`) as its prompt (`<|startofprev|>`), and detects the spoken language itself. transformers.js otherwise forces English on multilingual Whisper.
  - Recordings over 30 s are split into windows. Moonshine has no prompt.
- **Engine**: `localSpeech(ref, runner)` plugs into PR 1's registry. `batchEngines(settings)` now takes the settings. A missing, invalid or failing model falls back to OpenAI with the `fellBack` note, as before.
- **Models**: Moonshine Base (67 MB, English), Whisper Base (80 MB, multilingual incl. German), Whisper Small (252 MB, multilingual) and Distil-Whisper (175 MB, English).
  - Each is pinned to a Hugging Face revision, with every file's size and hash (SHA-256 for LFS files, git blob SHA-1 for small ones).
  - The download manager writes `.part` files, resumes with `Range` (and restarts if the server ignores it), and verifies each file before renaming it into place.
  - Models live in `MONEO_DATA_DIR/speech-models`: `.data/speech-models` on the source install, `<home>/data/speech-models` on desktop.
- **Your own model**: a folder holding a Whisper or Moonshine ONNX model. The folder is checked for `config.json` `model_type`, the tokenizer and preprocessor files, and an encoder/decoder pair in q8, fp32 or fp16.
- **Settings → Voice**: "On this computer" is selectable.
  - The model list shows size, languages and speed, with Download, progress and Retry.
  - "A model you already have": a native **Choose folder…** dialog on desktop (through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`, refused from a phone because the dialog would open on the computer), or a path field on the source install. Either way, it shows whether a model was found.
  - **Try it** records a sentence and shows what the model heard and how long it took. It calls `/api/voice/models/try`, which reports failures instead of falling back.
- **Stored choice**: `workspace_settings.speech_local_model` (migration `202611160227_speech_local_model.sql`, `save_workspace_preferences` updated, `lib/schema.ts` aligned). Reset all data deletes the settings row, so it clears the choice. It never touches model files.
- **Desktop**:
  - `next.config.ts` traces this platform's onnxruntime-node binary and onnxruntime-common into the standalone server. transformers.js loads them with `createRequire`, so they weren't traced. `build.mjs` fails if the binary is missing.
  - Models are not added to backup/restore: backups hold the database, storage and config only, and models can be downloaded again (noted in `desktop/src/backend/README.md`).
  - `fetch-backend.mjs` needs no change. The native module ships inside the app's `node_modules`, not as a backend service. Fuses are untouched.
- **Source install**: plain `npm ci` works. A new `.npmrc` sets `onnxruntime-node-install=skip` so Linux doesn't download the optional CUDA provider (hundreds of MB) on every install. No new environment variable. README explains downloading and choosing a model.

## Decisions to check

- **q8 for every model, so sizes differ from the issue's estimates** (Whisper Base 80 MB instead of ~150, Whisper Small 252 MB instead of ~500). On this machine, Whisper Base q8 was faster than fp16 (3.6 s vs 4.4 s warm for 7.4 s of audio) with the same or better text, at half the size. onnxruntime's CPU backend gains nothing from fp16.
- **"Choose folder…" instead of "Choose file…"**: transformers.js models are several files (config, tokenizer, two ONNX files), so the owner picks the folder.
- **Intel Macs can't run it**: onnxruntime-node 1.30 ships no darwin-x64 binary. Settings says so, and the mic falls back to OpenAI. The mac-x64 desktop build still builds (the binary check only runs where onnxruntime has one).

## How I verified it

- `npm test`: 316 files, 1805 tests passed. New tests:
  - Download manager: fake fetch, full download, resume with `Range`, server ignoring `Range`, hash mismatch never installed, one download per model with progress.
  - Engine selection: fake model runner, own folder, downloaded and partly downloaded suggested models, invalid folders, model failure, all through `transcribeWithFallback`.
  - Worker runner: idle unload, never while busy, crash recovery.
  - Routes: models list and download, try (no fallback), folder picker (desktop only, refused from a phone).
  - Also the bridge route and the settings action.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` (no warnings) and `npm run check:bundle` pass. `/settings` is 282 KB of a 298 KB budget.
- `npm run desktop:build` (Windows) passes. Its `node_modules` runs the packaged worker with Moonshine.
- `lib/schema.live.test.ts` passes against moneo-qa with the migration applied. I then reverted the migration on the shared QA database: column dropped, PR 1's function restored, migration row removed.
- **Real models**: `scripts/speech-model-check.mts` downloads a model (hash-checked) and transcribes WAVs, for manual use. With a TTS recording of "I spent twelve euros forty at Netto for groceries, and moved two hundred euros from my Girokonto to Revolut":
  - Moonshine: "…at netto … from my geariken to to revelu", 1.3 s warm.
  - Whisper Base fp16 with the names as prompt: "…at Netto for groceries, and moved 200 euros from Girokonto to Revolut.", 4.4 s.
  - Whisper Base q8: the same text, 3.6 s.
  - The owner's-own-folder path worked with an absolute Windows path.
- **In the QA app**:
  - Downloaded Moonshine and Whisper Base from Settings (progress shown), selected Moonshine and saved. "Preferences saved", and the choice was still there after a reload.
  - **Try it** through Chromium's fake microphone playing the recording: "I spent 12 euros 40 at netto…" in 2.3 s.
  - `/api/voice/session` returned `{"mode":"batch","engine":"local","fellBack":false}` and `/api/voice/transcribe` returned the text with `engine: "local"`.
  - No console errors or failed requests.

### Speech to text on this computer (optional)

The chat microphone can turn speech into text on the computer that runs Moneo, so recordings never leave it. It works from your phone too, because the model runs on the computer.

1. In **Settings → Voice**, set **Speech to text** to **On this computer**.
2. Click **Download** next to a model. Moonshine Base (67 MB) and Distil-Whisper (175 MB) understand English; Whisper Base (80 MB) and Whisper Small (252 MB) understand many languages, including German. Moonshine is the fastest, Whisper Small the most accurate. Models are saved in `.data/speech-models` (in the desktop app, in its data folder) and downloaded once from Hugging Face; each file is checked against its known size and hash, and a stopped download continues where it left off.
3. Or choose **A model you already have**: a folder holding a Whisper or Moonshine model in ONNX format (`config.json`, the tokenizer files and an `onnx` folder), such as one from [onnx-community](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community). Type its full path, or click **Choose folder…** in the desktop app.
4. Click **Try it**, say a sentence and check the text, then **Save preferences**.

The model loads the first time you use the mic and is unloaded after five idle minutes. Moneo passes the names of your accounts, shops and categories to Whisper models so they spell them right. Intel Macs can't run these models yet. If the model is missing or fails, Moneo uses OpenAI when you have added a key, and says so. Downloaded models aren't part of backups and stay when you reset your data; delete the folder to remove them.

### Speech to text with OpenRouter (optional)

The chat microphone can use any OpenRouter model that accepts audio, billed to your OpenRouter key. It needs no OpenAI key.
